rules.title: Dispose Pattern
rules.check: Classes with unmanaged resources MUST implement IDisposable correctly.

rules.title: Using Statement
rules.check: Always use using statement/declaration for IDisposable.
rules.bad_example:
var stream = new FileStream("data.bin", FileMode.Open);
stream.Read(buffer); // If exception throws, stream is never closed
rules.good_example:
using var stream = new FileStream("data.bin", FileMode.Open);
stream.Read(buffer);

rules.title: Span for Buffer Operations
rules.check: Use Span<T> over array copies for buffers.
rules.bad_example:
byte[] slice = new byte[10];
Array.Copy(buffer, 0, slice, 0, 10); // Allocates

rules.title: MemoryPool for Large Buffers
rules.bad_example: byte[] huge = new byte[100000]; // Goes to LOH (Slow GC)
rules.good_example:
using var owner = MemoryPool<byte>.Shared.Rent(100000);
var huge = owner.Memory;

rules.title: Stackalloc Limits
rules.check: stackalloc MUST NOT exceed 1024 bytes (Stack Overflow risk).

rules.title: No Finalizers Without Necessity
rules.check: Do NOT add a destructor (~Class()) unless strictly wrapping unmanaged handles.

rules.title: GC.SuppressFinalize
rules.check: If you have a finalizer, Dispose() MUST call GC.SuppressFinalize(this).
rules.bad_example: public void Dispose() { FreeNative(); } // GC still runs finalizer later

rules.title: WeakReference for Caches
rules.check: Long-lived caches SHOULD use WeakReference to avoid memory leaks.
rules.bad_example: static Dictionary<string, User> _cache; // Holds references forever

rules.title: No Closure Allocations in Hot Paths
rules.check: Lambdas in hot paths MUST NOT capture local variables (Allocates delegate + closure).
rules.bad_example:
int id = 5;
_cache.GetOrAdd(key, k => new Item(id)); // Captures 'id', allocates closure
rules.good_example:
int id = 5;
_cache.GetOrAdd(key, static (k, arg) => new Item(arg), id); // Static lambda, no allocation

rules.title: RecyclableMemoryStream
rules.check: High-throughput code MUST use RecyclableMemoryStream over MemoryStream.
rules.bad_example: using var ms = new MemoryStream(); // Allocates buffer every request

rules.title: Object Pooling
rules.check: Frequently allocated objects in hot paths SHOULD use ObjectPool<T>.
rules.bad_example:
// In request handler - allocates StringBuilder per request
var sb = new StringBuilder();

rules.title: Pinned Object Management
rules.check: GCHandle.Alloc with Pinned MUST be released in finally block. Prefer fixed statement.
